{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mi-s","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3f993c67a3166912c2ad7e667eb99d458bdf999c9033f367d834d5f66c07a599","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mi-class-std:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"7af7437894a2c63b20529c8a1ed7c10696796036051dd6666178ab579008ca37","source_liveness_sha256":"e81e5179580dc89fb25fdf5194e9f75291db3aa019fc21ccfe32c38d1a9df42f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals","heading":"C2 — Turn arrows, pedestrian signals, confusables and KG hints","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Turn arrows, pedestrian signals, confusables and KG hints

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A05
On a doghouse signal, a yellow light or yellow arrow means red is coming, so stop unless you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely; if already in, finish the turn with care once traffic is clear. [A05]
Why it matters: group turn signals; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec11-F33, sec11-F34 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A05
At a red light, stop completely and check cross traffic and pedestrians before moving on green or turning right on red. [A05]
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec11-F29 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A05
A flashing red light means come to a full stop and go only when the road is clear. [A05]
Why it matters: group flashing signals; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec11-R04 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A05
A flashing yellow light means go through the intersection carefully, scanning cross traffic both ways. [A05]
Why it matters: group flashing signals; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec11-R03 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A05
A steady green arrow means oncoming traffic is stopped and you may go the arrow's way with caution, still yielding to pedestrians in the intersection. [A05]
Why it matters: group turn signals; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec11-F34 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A05
The flashing yellow arrow left-turn signal uses four separate lenses, a design federal highway research found moves traffic more efficiently and cuts crash chances. [A05]
Why it matters: group flashing yellow arrow; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables none [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A05
A solid red arrow means stop and do not turn until the signal changes. [A05]
Why it matters: group flashing yellow arrow; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec11-R08 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A05
A solid yellow arrow warns the left-turn signal is about to turn red; stop if approaching, but if already in the intersection with no conflicting traffic you may finish the turn. [A05]
Why it matters: group flashing yellow arrow; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec11-R09 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A05
A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn left only after yielding to oncoming traffic, which has a green light, and after checking for a safe gap and for crossing pedestrians and bicyclists. [A05]
Why it matters: group flashing yellow arrow; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec11-R08, sec11-R10 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A05
A solid green arrow means oncoming traffic is stopped and you may turn left, still yielding to people in the crosswalk; with detection cameras or sensors this phase may be skipped when no one is waiting to turn. [A05]
Why it matters: group flashing yellow arrow; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec11-R09 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A05
Pedestrian signals control crossing points, and some show audible or visual countdowns of the time left. [A05]
Why it matters: group pedestrian signals; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables none [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A05
A walking person symbol or WALK means traffic must yield and pedestrians may cross; when it starts flashing, those already crossing should finish. [A05]
Why it matters: group pedestrian signals; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec11-R13 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A05
DONT WALK or a red raised hand means do not cross, and drivers must always yield to pedestrians. [A05]
Why it matters: group pedestrian signals; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec11-R12 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R14 | anchor: A06
A Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon is a crossing device that warns drivers of pedestrians, and its signal sequence has six steps. [A06]
Why it matters: group pedestrian signals; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec11-R15 | anchor: A05
A steady yellow on a doghouse signal means stop if you have not entered the intersection, whereas a flashing yellow light lets you continue carefully through it. [A05]
Why it matters: group signals; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec11-F30, sec11-R04 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec11-R16 | anchor: A03
A left-turn-only center lane has solid yellow lines on its outer edges and broken yellow lines on its inner edges, and it serves left turns from either direction but never passing or merging. [A03]
Why it matters: group yellow lines; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec11-F18 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-R17 | anchor: A02
A broken yellow center line allows passing when safe, but a solid yellow line on your side forbids it, and a double solid yellow forbids it for both directions. [A02]
Why it matters: group yellow lines; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec11-F14, sec11-F15, sec11-F17 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-R18 | anchor: A02
Any yellow line, whether solid, broken or a center-lane line, separates traffic moving in opposite directions. [A02]
Why it matters: group line colors; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec11-F13 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec11-R19 | anchor: A03
A Michigan Left crossover with no markings is always single-lane, even if it looks wide enough for two cars, because that width is for large vehicles. [A03]
Why it matters: group Michigan Lefts; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec11-F21, sec11-F22 [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec11-R20 | anchor: A04
White triangles across a lane are pedestrian yield lines, while dashed white lines across a roundabout lane mark the edge of the circle. [A04]
Why it matters: group yield lines; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec11-F26, sec11-F27 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0063]
